what: Owens Corning makes building materials: fibreglass insulation, roofing shingles, and since 2024 the Doors business bought from Masonite. It sold its glass fibre composites arm.
customers: Roofing contractors, insulation installers, builders and distributors in North America and Europe.
money: the largest part and most of the profit
interior and exterior doors, acquired in 2024
moat: Shingle plants close to their markets and a brand contractors ask for, in a roofing market where most demand is replacement after storms rather than new construction.
risks: A $427M net loss after write-downs on the Doors acquisition
New housing construction has been weak
opportunities: $767M of free cash flow at about 11 times cash flow, despite the accounting loss
Analysts see about 24% upside, with 16 covering the stock
Roofing is mostly storm-driven replacement, which does not depend on the housing cycle
watch: Roofing shingle volumes and whether the Doors business stabilises.
